family_context: Fictional parent whose adult child with co-occurring mental health and substance use needs is being discharged from an ER today with nowhere to go
immediate_goal: Stop a discharge to the street
information_to_confirm: Whether discharge can wait until a written plan exists and whether a treatment or respite bed can take them today
safe_next_step: Ask the hospital for its discharge plan in writing and call 988 about same-day co-occurring options before anyone leaves the building
if_entry_needed: One Roof Coordinated Entry only if every treatment door is closed today
handoff_owner: hospital discharge planner or social worker
takeover_point: The moment a treatment intake accepts them the intake staff own the plan

family_context: Fictional family that has reached the point where their person cannot stay in the home tonight and everyone is exhausted
immediate_goal: Get through tonight without the street
information_to_confirm: Whether mobile crisis or a crisis bed is available tonight and what 211 shows for tonight in your ZIP
safe_next_step: Call or text 988 before anyone packs a bag and say you are a family member in a co-occurring crisis
if_entry_needed: One Roof Coordinated Entry if no crisis option exists tonight
takeover_point: The counselor owns the next step from the moment they answer

family_context: Fictional family whose person left a detox program early and they are afraid the street comes next
immediate_goal: Get back into treatment before housing breaks
information_to_confirm: Whether the program will readmit them and exactly what the intake requires this time
safe_next_step: Search FindTreatment.gov for co-occurring programs and call the top matches before driving anywhere
if_entry_needed: One Roof Coordinated Entry if readmission fails and home is no longer possible
takeover_point: Intake staff take over at the first returned phone call

family_context: Fictional family holding an eviction notice while their person manages both a mental health condition and substance use
immediate_goal: Keep the housing so the system is never needed
information_to_confirm: What documents legal aid needs and every date printed on the notice
safe_next_step: Start Legal Services Alabama intake and dial 2-1-1 about rent and utility help before the court date
if_entry_needed: One Roof Coordinated Entry if the housing is lost anyway
takeover_point: Legal aid owns the case once intake accepts it
follow_up_window: before the date on the notice

family_context: Fictional family whose person cycles between jail the ER and the street and nothing has stuck
immediate_goal: Get one accountable owner instead of another loop
information_to_confirm: Whether your person is in JBS Mental Health Authority's service area and what its intake requires

if_entry_needed: One Roof Coordinated Entry whenever the street is where a loop ends
handoff_owner: JBS intake then an assigned case manager
takeover_point: A case manager owns the whole picture once assigned

family_context: Fictional family whose person refuses all help and the family is running out of strength
immediate_goal: Keep the family strong enough to catch the next opening
information_to_confirm: When the next NAMI family support group meets near you and whether 988 counsels family callers in this situation
safe_next_step: Join a NAMI Alabama family group and call 988 yourself because family callers count

handoff_owner: the family with NAMI support behind them
